# omadafusion_wireguard (Resource)

A WireGuard VPN interface on the gateway (VPN > WireGuard). Add peers with `omadafusion_wireguard_peer`. When `private_key` is omitted the controller generates a key pair; the private key is stored in state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "omadafusion_wan_ports" "this" {}

# Remote-access VPN on the gateway. The controller generates the key pair;
# give public_key to clients.
resource "omadafusion_wireguard" "remote" {
  name        = "remote-access"
  listen_port = 51820
  local_ip    = "10.250.0.1"
}

output "wireguard_public_key" {
  value = omadafusion_wireguard.remote.public_key
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `listen_port` (Number) UDP listen port on the WAN, 1-65535.
- `local_ip` (String) Tunnel address of the gateway, e.g. `10.250.0.1`.
- `name` (String) Interface name. Must be unique.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the interface is up.
- `mtu` (Number) Interface MTU, 576-1440.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) Base64 private key. Generated by the controller when omitted.
- `site` (String) Site name or ID. Defaults to the provider `site`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Interface ID.
- `public_key` (String) Public key to give to peers.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <id> or <site>/<id>
terraform import omadafusion_wireguard.remote Default/64f0c0ffee00000000000010
```
